values: Static code review - evidence-based findings from repository inspection. Scope: backend APIs/controllers/services, frontend controls and data flow. Runtime/database/browser integration remains pending.
Only an authenticated, authorized user can delete a complaint through a POST request protected against cross-site request forgery.
Deletes a complaint when a GET id is supplied; starts a session but never checks user or role. A crafted link can trigger deletion for a logged-in user.
Require POST, enforce Administrator/Lupon Clerk authorization, add CSRF validation, validate the ID, return a JSON result, and retain an audit record before deletion.
Archive changes must be limited to authorized users and use an explicit protected mutation request.
Accepts an id from GET or POST, performs no role check, and archives any valid complaint. The session is not used to authorize the action.
Accept only POST, require the same role gate used by other complaint mutations, add CSRF protection, and reject missing or invalid IDs with 422.
Case archival must authenticate the actor, validate the request method and case ID, and report failure accurately.
Reads $_POST['case_id'] directly without a method check, session initialization, authorization, or input validation. The controller audit may reference an unset session user.
Start the session, require POST and an authorized role, validate case_id with FILTER_VALIDATE_INT, return meaningful HTTP/JSON responses, and apply CSRF protection.
A save response must reflect the result of a validated, authorized controller operation.

Has no session or role check and always returns success after calling a non-existent SettlementController::create() method. This produces a fatal error or a false success contract depending on runtime handling.
Retire or replace this route with SettlementController::save(), require authentication/RBAC/CSRF, validate input, and propagate the controller result and status code.
Only authorized users can create an arbitration award and API output must reflect persistence success.
No session or role check; always emits a success JSON payload even if ArbitrationController::create() returns false or throws.
Require POST, RBAC and CSRF; validate request data; inspect the controller result and return 4xx/5xx failure payloads instead of unconditional success.
Sensitive complaint, party, attachment, and case data must require an authenticated authorized session.
Returns ComplaintController::show() without starting or checking a session. The controller includes parties, attachments, documents and workflow data.
Require authenticated role-based access before loading the complaint and enforce record-level authorization if access is scoped by case/team.
Case details should validate IDs and require an authorized reader.
No session/RBAC check; directly reads $_GET['id'] and returns the case controller result. An unset id also generates a PHP notice.
Start the session, validate id, return 422 for invalid input, and require an authorized role before querying the case.
Dashboard data should be restricted to signed-in roles and fail safely.
No session or role check before ReportController::dashboard() is called, exposing aggregate operational data to unauthenticated requests.
Apply the dashboard role gate before controller construction and use a consistent JSON error response for unauthenticated/unauthorized callers.
AI requests must require authentication, POST-only access, input length validation, and rate limits before sending data to an external provider.
Both routes lack session/RBAC, method checks, request validation, and rate limiting. Any caller can trigger provider requests, and narrative input may include sensitive complaint details.
Route through the hardened refine-narrative pattern: authenticate/authorize, validate bounded payloads, rate limit, document consent/privacy handling, and return controlled errors.
Missing optional narrative fields should be handled without PHP notices and untrusted text should be bounded before prompt construction.
Interpolates $data['who'], ['what'], ['when'], ['where'], ['why'], and ['how'] directly. Missing fields generate notices and unbounded input is sent to the AI service.
Use null-coalescing defaults, validate per-field types and lengths, and use the documented refineNarrative-style prompt boundaries.
Raw base64 uploads should be decoded, size-limited, and rejected before large allocations or provider requests.

For string/base64 inputs, transcribeAudio() and ocrImage() accept the string without decoding or enforcing the documented 25 MB/15 MB limits. A large JSON body can consume application and provider resources.
Validate allowed MIME types, estimate/decode base64 safely, enforce byte limits before request construction, and configure PHP request-size limits.
Internal failure details should not be returned to clients, and scheduling constraints should be safe under concurrent requests.

Exception handlers append $exception->getMessage() to the user response, leaking database or implementation details. Conflict checking occurs before persistence, so concurrent requests can both pass unless the model/database enforces the same constraint transactionally.

Log detailed exceptions server-side and return a generic message with an error ID. Enforce final conflict/capacity validation inside the write transaction and add supporting uniqueness/locking where appropriate.
Hearing schedules should not be created in the past unless an authorized exception is explicitly recorded.
The source explicitly states that the future date restriction is bypassed for testing/development, leaving production behavior dependent on other checks.
Restore server-side future-date validation with a narrowly scoped authorized override that records actor, reason, and audit history.
Availability data should use the same role gate as the scheduling interface.
Endpoint requires only user_id, unlike create/update/cancel which require Administrator or Lupon Clerk. This may disclose officer, venue, or schedule availability to roles that cannot schedule.
Confirm the intended policy. If availability is operationally sensitive, require roles 1/2 or return a reduced availability response for other roles.
Drafts, minor guardians, categories, and jurisdiction screening
Drafts may remain incomplete; submitted complaints must validate category, narrative, parties, guardian requirements, map/location, jurisdiction screen, and duplicate acknowledgement.
Reviewed implementation performs model-side validation for non-drafts and preserves draft behavior. Duplicate acknowledgement and jurisdiction screen are also checked on the server.
Keep validation centralized in Complaint and add automated API coverage for the permitted draft and blocked submission paths.
Uploads must validate files before moving them, use controlled storage paths, and remove partial files on failure.
Reviewed ComplaintController attachment workflow validates uploaded files and cleans up a target file on database failure; download endpoint constrains resolved paths to approved upload directories.
Add malware scanning and content-disposition hardening only if deployment policy requires it.
Scheduling controls and async API responses
Mutating hearing controls should accept only authorized POST requests and return a consistent success/failure response.
Reviewed endpoints enforce POST and roles 1/2, validate hearing IDs where applicable, and return JSON status payloads consumed by the scheduling UI.
Add end-to-end browser tests for disabled buttons, conflict messages, and retry behavior after a network error.
User-derived text must be escaped before insertion into HTML; actions should not interpolate untrusted values into executable attributes.

The reviewed primary screens frequently use innerHTML. Many visible fields are escaped, but the large codebase needs a focused taint review for every interpolated attribute/URL and inline onclick handler before declaring it XSS-safe.

Standardize a DOM rendering helper, continue using escapeHtml for text, validate URL schemes/IDs separately, and add automated XSS payload tests for complaint, resident, document, and notification data.
State-changing requests should verify a CSRF token or equivalent same-site anti-forgery mechanism.
No shared CSRF middleware or token verification was found during the endpoint review; several mutations rely only on cookies/session state.
Add a centralized CSRF token issue/validation middleware, include the token in all forms and fetch requests, and test rejection of missing/invalid tokens.
Backend PHP files and frontend JavaScript files should parse before release.
A full lint pass was initiated, but the command produced no captured per-file output in this execution environment. This does not establish an integration pass.
Run PHP lint over every PHP file and node --check over every JavaScript file in CI, fail the build on any error, and retain the log as a release artifact.
